title: Inner Sanctum Mysteries
paragraphs: A horror and mystery anthology famous for its creaking-door opening, mixing murder, supernatural menace, psychological terror, and darkly playful host narration.

Himan Brown horror-mystery anthology framed by the creaking Inner Sanctum door and a macabre host. Frozen GRH snapshot contains 155 playable objects through September 28, 1952 plus one undated Judas Clock variant.

GRH documents the program through Blue Network era (January 7, 1941 to August 29, 1943) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], CBS long era (September 4, 1943 to April 17, 1950) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], ABC era (September 4, 1950 to June 18, 1951) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], and Final CBS era (June 22, 1952 to October 5, 1952) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|paul-mcgrath|Paul McGrath]] (host on 101 recordings and performer on 1 recording), Santos Ortega (performer on 53 recordings), Everett Sloane (performer on 37 recordings), Himan Brown (director on 35 recordings, producer on 3 recordings, and creator on 1 recording), Mary Bennett (commercial spokesman on 20 recordings and commercial spokeswoman on 10 recordings), Lawson Zerbe (performer on 26 recordings), and [[person|raymond-edward-johnson|Raymond Edward Johnson]] (host on 26 recordings and performer on 1 recording).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include murder and homicide, corpses, burial and the dead, ghosts and returns from the grave, madness and psychological instability, fraud, insurance and deception, and revenge and retribution.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Radio horror anthology tradition, The creaking door as sonic branding, Macabre host versus commercial spokeswoman, and 1952 revival through script reuse.
